summary: Realtime translation streams collapsing under failover causing dropped context and customer escalation
description: Issue summary: LinguaStream reported that live translation sessions intermittently dropped mid-stream during an automated failover window, causing lost conversation context and user-visible truncation. Impact: Live subtitles and translated captions were missing or truncated for ~12 minutes across several customer sessions; customer reported immediate business impact on live event broadcasts. Environment: Production, us-west primary, failover to eu-west attempted during autoscaler activity. Timeline: 03/10 09:12 UTC first alerts; 09:14 UTC customer escalation to #support; 09:20 UTC observed elevated reconnects and truncated transcripts; 09:26 UTC emergency rollback of routing policy; 09:34 UTC customer observed recovery.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Open long-lived streaming session to translation endpoint using session-affinity cookie and streaming proxy. 2) Trigger autoscaler drain of a serving pool (simulate node restart) or force a routing-variant fallback. 3) Observe that client reconnects but resumed stream lacks prefix context and returns truncated completions. 4) Repeat with model variant mismatch (quantized vs full-precision) to reproduce context loss.

comments: Tom A (support): Customer reported truncated captions during a live broadcast at 09:12 UTC; escalated to SRE.
#support (Slack): Noted elevated reconnects and a pattern where resumed streams returned empty prefixes; correlates with an autoscale event in us-west.
SRE (Aisha K): Reproduced locally by forcing routing fallback; observed session-affinity token not propagated to fallback worker which triggers KV cache miss and silent truncation.
Customer CS rep (Marta P): LinguaStream confirmed recovery after rollback and requested credits and a technical writeup of root cause and mitigations.
Aisha K (SRE): Emergency change rolled back routing policy at 09:26 UTC to maintain model-variant pinning; raised INT-3321 for a durable fix.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: aggressive fallback policy combined with streaming-proxy reconnect logic allowed client reconnections to be routed to a model variant that did not share prefix KVs, causing resumed sessions to treat the request as cold-start. Evidence: paired logs show conn reset followed by KV_CACHE_MISS for the same session-id and immediate fallback-to-variant event. Additional observation: when fallback target was quantized variant, the runtime accepted resume tokens but did not map KV namespaces correctly due to a recent change that allowed variant-specific prefix namespaces. Load testing reproduced the issue when failover rate > 30% within 60s. Related code path: streaming-proxy session reattach and runtime model-variant namespace mapping (commit 1a9f3c8 changed mapping behavior).
resolution_notes: Immediate mitigation: rolled back routing-policy change and disabled aggressive variant fallback for translation model family, restoring session-affinity and pinning to compatible variants. Patch deployed to streaming-proxy to preserve session-id to KV-namespace mapping across reconnects (PR #612). Post-incident deployment included canary in us-west for 24h. Customer compensation: one month's service credit applied and technical debrief scheduled. Long-term actions: 1) Add end-to-end integration test for streaming reconnection with variant fallback. 2) Modify runtime to normalize prefix namespaces across compatible model variants or provide clear fallback semantics. 3) Update runbook and add alert for 'KV_CACHE_MISS with session reconnects' (owner: SRE). 4) Validate autoscaler and routing interactions in chaos tests.
post_incident_actions: Action: Add e2e streaming reconnection test that simulates variant fallback (owner: QA, due: 2026-04-02)
Action: Implement runtime normalization for prefix namespaces or explicit session-migration logic (owner: Serving Runtime eng, due: 2026-05-15)
Action: Update routing policy defaults to require session-affinity preservation for translation model family (owner: Routing team, due: 2026-03-20)
Action: Create dashboard and alert for 'session reconnects + KV_CACHE_MISS' and tie to Pager duty (owner: Observability, due: 2026-03-18)
Action: Customer debrief and postmortem presentation scheduled (owner: CS, due: 2026-03-17)
Action: Runbook note: for live event customers, avoid variant fallback during scheduled broadcasts; provide a safeguard flag (owner: Solutions Eng, due: 2026-04-01)
customer_communication: Initial: Acknowledge within 30m and place on priority queue (09:15 UTC). Update at 09:30 UTC: informed of rollback and mitigation; provided ETA for root cause analysis. Final: sent technical postmortem and credits on 2026-03-12; scheduled live runbook review with LinguaStream for 2026-03-17.
resolution: Patch and routing rollback applied; monitoring shows no recurrences in 72h window. Customer accepts postmortem and credits.
notes_for_followup_call: Be prepared to show the reconstructed timeline, explain namespace mapping root cause, walk through the patch PR, and discuss schedule for longer-term runtime change. Confirm LinguaStream's planned broadcast calendar to avoid planned change windows.
